jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Tennessee, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Tennessee, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, Tennessee Senate, Tennessee House and U.S. House districts, cities and towns, school districts and ZIP codes.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 9 congressional districts — the largest districts Tennessee carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 9 features for Tennessee, measured 2026-10-10. The layer's own district field is CD119. THIS IS THE MAP THE SITTING MEMBERS WERE ELECTED FROM, NOT THE NEWEST ONE: Tennessee redrew its districts in 2026, and layer 0 (the 120th Congress) moves 39.9% of the state's area to another district, so drawing it beside these members would name the wrong representative for most of Memphis. The switch to layer 0 is due on 3 January 2027, when the members elected from it take their seats, and the builder refuses to rebuild layer 4 from that date.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Tennessee Senate District
layers.rank_note: 33 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Tennessee Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 33 features, measured 2026-10-10. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 20 m interval and refused over a 25 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: tn-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI. The NAME and whether the seat is vacant come from the Tennessee Legislature's own district map on the state's TNMap service; party, e-mail and the member's own page come from the Open States export, and only where its member for the district has the same surname. Neither source carries a capitol office or telephone, and the Legislature's own site refuses automated readers in its robots.txt, so it is linked from the card and never read.

source.answers: Which county contains the point, and whether that county is consolidated with its principal city.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 95 features, measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: None yet — identity only. Every Tennessee county elects its legislative body from districts, and the Comptroller of the Treasury publishes every county's districts in one statewide service; no state office publishes the members' names, and neither is wired in this first change. Recorded as gap tn-county-commission-districts.

layers.label: School District (Unified)
layers.rank_note: 127 unified districts, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file); with the 15 elementary districts they cover the state exactly

source.answers: The public school district covering the point, where one district runs every grade.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), queried live at runtime; 127 features for Tennessee, measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD SAYS SO. Tennessee's school boards are elected, and no statewide roster of their members was established in this pass; the card names the district, prints the grades the Census records and links the state Department of Education's school directory. Recorded as gap tn-school-board-members.
source.applies: Tennessee — every point outside the 15 city and special school districts. The unified and elementary tilings partition the state: their Census land areas sum to exactly the 95-county total, measured 2026-10-10.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 1,070 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas in the state's own bounding box, fetched live by envelope; the layer hides outside Tennessee

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, queried live at runtime. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='47'. 1,070 features in Tennessee's box, measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Tennessee. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code (Bowling Green, Kentucky gives 42101).

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), queried live at runtime; 345 features for Tennessee (182 cities, 160 towns and 3 consolidated governments), measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Tennessee's cities and towns elect councils and boards, and no statewide roster was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap tn-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: Tennessee — statewide. A point outside every city and town is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-10: 503 points in Tennessee's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Tennessee — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: the State Capitol, Nashville, Davidson County

negative_point.note: near Hazel Green, Madison County, ALABAMA, about 11 km south of the state line — outside Tennessee and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate (minLat 34.80) so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-10: TIGERweb's state layer names Alabama at this point (control: the Capitol anchor returns Tennessee). ALABAMA BECAUSE NO INSTANCE SERVES IT and none is planned next: Arkansas and Mississippi, both on the next-states list, were passed over so this point does not have to move when either goes live.
